overview.headline: Unpowered glider glide angle and lift drag equilibrium in steady descent

keyPoints.point: A glider is a special aircraft with no engine and must be launched externally
keyPoints.quote: A glider is a special kind of aircraft that has no engine.

keyPoints.point: The flight path intersects the ground at an angle called the glide angle describing steady descent
keyPoints.quote: The flight path intersects the ground at an angle a called the glide angle.

keyPoints.point: The tangent of the glide angle equals height change divided by distance flown
keyPoints.quote: The tangent tan of the glide angle a is equal to the change in height h divided by the distance flown d:

keyPoints.point: Lift and drag components along the glide angle balance the weight in steady flight
keyPoints.quote: The lift L times the cosine cos of the glide angle plus the drag D times the sine sin of the glide angle is equal to the weight W:

keyTerms.gloss: An aircraft with no engine that must be launched to fly
keyTerms.quote: A glider is a special kind of aircraft that has no engine.

keyTerms.gloss: Angle between the steady flight path and the ground determining descent
keyTerms.quote: The flight path intersects the ground at an angle a called the glide angle.

keyTerms.gloss: Ratio of height change to distance describing the glide angle
keyTerms.quote: The tangent tan of the glide angle a is equal to the change in height h divided by the distance flown d:

keyTerms.gloss: Force that with drag balances weight along the glide angle through cosine component
keyTerms.quote: The lift L times the cosine cos of the glide angle plus the drag D times the sine sin of the glide angle is equal to the weight W:

keyTerms.gloss: Aerodynamic resistance balanced with lift through sine and glide angle components
keyTerms.quote: The lift times the sine of the glide angle is equal to the drag times the cosine of the glide angle.
